items.prompt: White is in check from the black rook. Could White simply play the rook from a8 to a7 and carry on, ignoring the check? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: White is in check.
The rook move a8-a7 leaves the king attacked, so it is illegal.

hints: After your move, would the black rook still be looking at the white king?
Does the rook move to a7 block the e-file, or take the rook?
A move that leaves your own king attacked is never allowed.
items.explain: The black rook still attacks the white king after the rook move to a7, because nothing blocks the e-file. A move that leaves your own king in check is illegal.

items.prompt: The black bishop gives check. Find a move that gets out of check without moving the king.

claims.statement: White is in check from the bishop.
White has exactly eight legal moves: one capture, three blocks and four king steps.
The pawn can capture the bishop.
The pawn can block on c3.
The knight can block on c3.
The knight can block on d2.

hints: There are three ways out of check. You may not move the king this time, so look for a block or a capture.
Follow the bishop's diagonal toward the king. Which squares lie between them, and who can reach them?
One pawn can take the bishop; a pawn and a knight can step onto the diagonal.
items.explain: The bishop attacks along the diagonal b4, c3, d2, e1. The pawn on a3 can capture it, and a pawn or the knight can step onto c3, or the knight onto d2, to block.

feedback_by_move.e1f1: That is a king move, and this question asks for a block or a capture.

items.prompt: A black queen gives check from the square next to the king. Can the white king capture it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: White is in check.
The king may capture the queen.
No black piece guards the queen's square.

hints: Ask: if the king takes the queen, would any black piece then attack the king?
Look at the squares around the queen. Does anything of Black guard d2?
Nothing guards d2, so the king is safe there.
items.explain: A king may capture an attacker next to it if no enemy piece guards that square. Nothing guards the queen, so the king takes it.

items.prompt: A black queen gives check from the square next to the king. Can the white king capture it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: White is in check.
Capturing on d2 is illegal because the knight guards it.
One black piece (the knight) attacks d2.
The king's only legal move is to f1.

hints: If the king took the queen, what would be attacking the king on d2?
Find the black piece that attacks d2 apart from the queen.
The knight on b3 attacks d2, so the king may not go there.
items.explain: The knight on b3 guards d2. A king may never move onto a square an enemy piece attacks, so capturing the queen is illegal and the king can only retreat to f1.

items.prompt: A black knight on e2 gives check. Tap every square the white king can step to.

claims.statement: White is in check from the knight.
The king has exactly three safe squares.

hints: The squares next to the king are f1, f2, g2, h1 and h2. Which are free?
Two of the neighbouring squares hold white pawns.
Check whether the knight on e2 attacks f1, f2 or h1.
items.explain: The pawns on g2 and h2 fill two squares. The knight attacks g1 and a few other squares, but not f1, f2 or h1, so those three are the king's exits.

items.prompt: Black is in check from the rook and the king has no safe square. Find a move that answers the check.

claims.statement: Black is in check.
Black has exactly two legal moves: the bishop captures the rook or blocks on f8.

hints: Count the king's free squares first. Are there any?
Which black piece can reach a square between the rook and the king, or take the rook?
A bishop on e7 reaches both d8 and f8.
items.explain: The king has no safe square, but the bishop can take the checking rook or step between rook and king. Either answers the check, so this is check but not mate.

items.prompt: Black is in check from the rook on d8. Find the only way out.

claims.statement: Black is in check.
Black has exactly one legal move, the bishop capture on d8.

hints: Is there a safe square for the king? Is there a piece that could block?
Look along the long diagonal from a5. Does a black piece see the white rook?
The black bishop on a5 can take the checking rook.
items.explain: The king has no safe square and nothing can step between, but Black's bishop sees the white rook along a diagonal and can capture it.

items.prompt: White to move. Is the white king in check, checkmated, or neither?

claims.statement: White is not in check.
White is free to move the king.

hints: A check needs an attacker with a clear line to the king.
Look at the e-file between the black rook and the white king.
The white knight on e3 stands in the way.
items.explain: The black rook points down the e-file, but the white knight on e3 stands in the way, so the king is not attacked. A line attacker needs a clear line.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is the black king in check, checkmated, or neither?

claims.statement: Black is checkmated.
Black has no legal move.

hints: Is the king attacked? Then test the three ways in turn.
Can the king capture the queen? Look at what guards the queen.
The white king guards b7, and the queen covers the other squares.
items.explain: The queen attacks the king and the white king guards the queen, so the black king cannot take it. The queen also covers a7 and b8, and nothing can block. That is checkmate.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is the black king in check, checkmated, or neither?

claims.statement: Black is in check.
Black's only legal move is the king capturing the queen.

hints: Is the king attacked? Then test the three ways in turn.
Can the king capture the queen? Look at what guards the queen.
Nothing guards b7, so the king may take it.
items.explain: The queen attacks the king, but nothing guards the queen, so the king captures it. It is check, not mate.

items.prompt: Both the rook and the knight give check at once (a double check). Find a legal move.

claims.statement: White is in check.
The only legal moves are the two king steps.

hints: One block or one capture could fix only one of the two checks.
Since the other check would remain, which piece must move?
The king steps to d2 or f1.
items.explain: The queen could capture the knight, but the rook would still give check. In a double check only a king move helps, and here the king has two safe squares.

items.prompt: The black rook gives check. Can the white knight on c3 block by moving to e2? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: White is in check.
The block on e2 is illegal because the knight is pinned to the king.
Only king steps are legal.

hints: If the knight leaves c3, which black piece suddenly attacks the king?
Follow the diagonal from b4 through c3 to e1.
The knight is pinned, so it may not move at all.
items.explain: The bishop on b4 attacks through the knight to the king. If the knight moved to e2 it would block the rook, but it would open the bishop's line, leaving the king attacked. A way out counts only if your king is safe afterwards.

items.prompt: The black rook gives check. Can the white knight on c3 block by moving to e2? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: White is in check.
The knight may block on e2.
Two blocks and four king steps are legal.

hints: If the knight leaves c3, does any black piece attack the king along another line?
Look for a black bishop or rook aimed at c3.
Nothing is aimed through c3, so the knight is free.
items.explain: Nothing pins the knight, so it can step onto e2 and block the rook. Compared with the other position, the only change is the missing bishop.
